title: Extract a reusable SettingsRow from renderPanel
description: Pull the inline row construction out of renderPanel in src/panel.js into an exported SettingsRow(key, value) that returns the .row element with its .row-label span and value span. renderPanel maps settings through it. No visual change: the same markup, same classes, same order.
acceptanceCriteria: SettingsRow(key, value) is exported from src/panel.js and returns a .row element containing a .row-label span with the key and a span with String(value)
renderPanel builds every row through SettingsRow and its rendered output is byte-identical to today's for the DEFAULTS settings object
rationale: Every later control mounts into a row; extracting the row shape once stops six tickets each forking the markup.

title: Persist settings to localStorage in store.js
description: Extend src/store.js with saveSettings(settings) writing JSON to localStorage under a single key, and make loadSettings read that key and merge it over DEFAULTS, falling back to DEFAULTS when the key is absent or unparseable. Storage access is wrapped so a throwing localStorage degrades to DEFAULTS rather than crashing boot.
acceptanceCriteria: saveSettings(settings) writes the settings as JSON to localStorage under one key
loadSettings merges the stored value over DEFAULTS; with no stored value, or an unparseable one, it returns DEFAULTS unchanged
A localStorage that throws on read or write leaves loadSettings returning DEFAULTS and does not throw
rationale: Persistence is pure store-layer work touching no DOM, so it is independent of the row foundation and of every control built on it.

title: Add a Reset to defaults button to the panel header
description: Add a panel header above the rows with a 'Reset to defaults' button. Clicking it restores DEFAULTS in memory and re-renders the rows. It does not yet confirm and does not yet persist beyond what t-002 already does.
acceptanceCriteria: The panel renders a header containing a button labelled 'Reset to defaults'
Clicking it restores every setting to its DEFAULTS value and the rendered rows update to match
rationale: A self-contained addition into the row foundation; independent of persistence and of the modal primitives.

title: Add overlay/modal CSS primitives and a Modal helper
description: src/styles.css has no .overlay, .modal or .modal-foot rule today. Add them — a dimmed full-screen .overlay, a centered .modal card, and a .modal-foot action row — plus a small Modal helper in a new src/modal.js that mounts a modal into the overlay and resolves on confirm or dismiss. No consumer in this ticket.
acceptanceCriteria: src/styles.css defines .overlay (a dimmed full-screen backdrop), .modal (a centered card) and .modal-foot (a right-aligned action row)
src/modal.js exports a Modal helper that mounts a modal inside the overlay and resolves true on confirm and false on dismiss
Nothing in the app opens a modal yet; the existing panel render is unchanged
rationale: The overlay/modal primitives are shared UI infrastructure with no consumer of their own; building them as their own slice keeps the confirmation modal from inventing a second styling path.

title: Render boolean settings as a toggle control
description: Inside SettingsRow, render a boolean value as a toggle input instead of the plain 'true'/'false' text, wired to update the in-memory settings and persist through t-002's saveSettings when present. Non-boolean values keep their current text rendering.
acceptanceCriteria: A boolean setting renders as a toggle control in its row rather than the text 'true' or 'false'
Toggling it updates the in-memory settings value and the row reflects the new state
A non-boolean setting's row is unchanged
rationale: A row-local control that changes only how one value type renders; independent of the reset button, the modal primitives and the banner.

title: Confirm before a reset discards settings
description: Make the Reset to defaults button open a confirmation modal — a centered modal over a dimmed backdrop, with a red Discard action (#modal-discard) and a Cancel — and only reset when Discard is chosen. Dismissing leaves the settings untouched.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking 'Reset to defaults' opens a centered modal over a dimmed backdrop carrying a red Discard action (#modal-discard) and a Cancel action
Choosing Discard restores DEFAULTS; choosing Cancel or dismissing leaves every setting untouched
rationale: A destructive action needs a confirmation step; it wires the reset flow into the shared modal rather than building a bespoke dialog.

title: Show an unsaved-changes banner
description: Add a banner above the rows shown when the in-memory settings differ from what is persisted in localStorage, and hidden when they match. It reads the persisted value through t-002's store API rather than touching localStorage directly.
acceptanceCriteria: When the in-memory settings differ from the persisted settings, a banner appears above the rows saying the changes are unsaved
When they match, no banner is rendered
rationale: The banner is a pure consumer of the persistence layer and of nothing else, so it is independent of every control built on the row foundation.

title: Add keyboard navigation across rows
description: Make rows focusable and navigable: arrow keys move focus between rows, Enter activates the row's control. Focus is visible via a focus style in src/styles.css.
acceptanceCriteria: Rows are focusable and ArrowDown / ArrowUp move focus to the next and previous row
Enter activates the focused row's control
The focused row carries a visible focus style
rationale: Navigation is a behaviour over the row foundation that touches no individual control's internals; it can be built alongside them.
